name: Body Joint Limit Analysis
description: Validates body joint angles against biomechanical constraints — AI often generates anatomically impossible poses.
mechanism:
This method checks whether the body poses in video frames respect the anatomical range of motion (ROM) limits of human joints:

1. **3D Pose Estimation and Joint Angle Computation**: The method extracts 3D body joint positions per frame using a monocular 3D pose estimator (e.g., MotionBERT or SPIN). From the 3D joint positions, joint angles are computed for all major articulations: shoulder flexion/extension, abduction/adduction, and internal/external rotation; elbow flexion; wrist flexion/extension and ulnar/radial deviation; hip flexion/extension, abduction/adduction; knee flexion; and ankle dorsiflexion/plantarflexion. The angles are computed using the anatomical coordinate frames defined by the International Society of Biomechanics (Wu et al., 2002). Each joint's degrees of freedom and their ranges are checked against established normative data.

2. **Range of Motion Violation Detection**: Each computed joint angle is compared against the biomechanical ROM limits derived from clinical anthropometric studies (Boone & Azen, 1979). Key constraints include: shoulder flexion 0–180°, shoulder abduction 0–180°, elbow flexion 0–145°, wrist flexion 0–80°, hip flexion 0–120°, knee flexion 0–135°, ankle dorsiflexion 0–20°. The method applies a tolerance margin of ±10° to account for pose estimation errors and individual variation. Violations exceeding this margin are flagged, with a severity score proportional to the angular overshoot. AI-generated video frequently produces poses where the elbow hyperextends beyond 0°, the knee bends backward, or the neck rotates beyond ~80°.

3. **Joint Coupling Constraint Verification**: Many joints have coupled constraints — the ROM of one joint depends on the configuration of adjacent joints. For example: (a) the elbow cannot fully extend when the forearm is fully pronated, (b) hip flexion ROM decreases when the knee is extended (hamstring tension), (c) lumbar lateral flexion is limited by concurrent rotation. The method encodes these coupling constraints as inequality functions and checks each frame. AI generators typically model joints independently, producing poses that violate these coupling relationships even when individual joint angles are within range.

4. **Temporal Joint Angle Smoothness**: In natural human motion, joint angles change smoothly with limited angular velocity and acceleration (constrained by muscle dynamics). The method computes joint angular velocity and acceleration from the temporal derivative of angle trajectories and flags: (a) instantaneous angle jumps (> 30°/frame at 30fps), (b) angular accelerations exceeding physiological limits (shoulder: ~5000°/s², elbow: ~8000°/s²), (c) jerk (rate of change of acceleration) that exceeds natural motion profiles. AI-generated video often produces jerky joint trajectories or instantaneous pose changes.
parameters:
Pose estimator: MotionBERT / SPIN
Joint angles computed: 22 DOF (major joints)
ROM tolerance margin: ±10°
Shoulder flexion limit: 0–180°
Elbow flexion limit: 0–145°
Knee flexion limit: 0–135°
Hip flexion limit: 0–120°
Angular velocity limit: 30°/frame at 30fps
Coupling constraints: 8 biomechanical pairs
Minimum video length: 10 frames
Frame rate: ≥ 24 fps
accuracy: 75–84% accuracy for detecting anatomically impossible poses in AI-generated video. Individual ROM violation detection achieves precision of 0.87. Joint coupling analysis adds 5–7% improvement for subtle violations. Temporal smoothness analysis achieves F1-score of 0.80 for detecting jerky motion. Performance depends on 3D pose estimation quality — errors in pose estimation can masquerade as joint violations.
source: Wu, G. et al. (2002). ISB Recommendation on Definitions of Joint Coordinate System of Various Joints for the Reporting of Human Joint Motion. Journal of Biomechanics, 35, 543–548.
useCase: Detecting AI-generated videos with anatomically impossible body poses. Verifying motion capture data quality. Forensic analysis of video evidence for deepfake detection. Quality assessment of character animation and pose estimation systems.
strengths:
• Anatomical ROM limits are well-established and objective
• Joint coupling constraints catch subtle violations that individual ROM checks miss
• Temporal analysis detects non-physical motion dynamics
• Works for any body pose — not limited to specific actions or activities
• Violations are physically interpretable and explainable
limitations:
• Monocular 3D pose estimation has inherent depth ambiguity — errors propagate to joint angles
• Flexible individuals (gymnasts, dancers) may have ROM exceeding normative values
• Loose clothing can obscure joint positions, leading to pose estimation errors
• Partial occlusion prevents analysis of occluded joints
• AI models trained on large motion capture datasets are improving their anatomical accuracy
